question: can the sign of the 558,005 unsigned curated regulatory edges be imputed, validated where it cannot be circular?

decision_threshold_fixed_before_run.increments_are_PAIRED: the arm and its swapped-source control are scored on the SAME rows; the unpaired construction is reported alongside for comparability with colab/causal_reg.py but governs nothing

label.definition: sign of per-gene robust z of K562 log fold change, as in causal_reg.py

degree_matched_rewiring.kind: configuration model; reg target+sign stubs permuted (out-degree and in-degree exact), ppi stub list permuted and re-paired, coexpr and complex incidence permuted

constructions: nn: +/-150 nearest in strength rank, added after the decile arm failed its own imbalance audit
joint: strength decile x library-size decile, added after the nn arm still left UMI count imbalanced

paired_vs_unpaired.why: conditioning the control on |z|>=2 moves it onto stress-responsive targets whose direction is more consistent; scoring the arm on all its rows against a control on that subset is not a comparison. The paired columns fix it and reverse the sign of the nearest-neighbour increment.

rpe1_class_prior.note: the majority class FLIPS between the lines, so the RPE1 accuracy readout measures the flip and not transfer; read the AUC columns

limits: ONLY 59.0% OF CURATED EDGES ARE TESTABLE AT ALL. K562 measures 8,248 genes and RPE1 8,749, so an edge whose target is unmeasured contributes to no number here -- it is neither signed nor counted as a failure, and the null is a null about the measurable majority only

the label is a K562 CRISPRi response, which is a causal consequence of knocking the source down and not evidence the source acts on the target. An indirect edge with a consistent sign is scored as a correct sign here

THE 'CEILING' IN SECTION 2 IS NOT SOURCE-LEVEL REGULATORY SIGNAL. Both halves come from the SAME perturbation row, so any global up/down shift of that row transfers between them perfectly. The non-target control added here settles it: a source's direction bias estimated from genes that are NOT its curated targets predicts its held-out true targets at least as well as the bias estimated from its own targets. The quantity is a property of the experiment, not of the TF, and no sequence feature could recover it

training labels are restricted to |z| >= 2, which conditions on the outcome magnitude. Every control arm is conditioned identically, but the population being predicted is 'edges whose target responds strongly', not all edges

the source+edge arm rests on ONE quantity with any prior claim to informativeness, the curated activator fraction, and it is finite on only 67.7% of the scored edges and 50.3% of their source genes -- NOT the 86.4% an earlier version of this module asserted -- and it is derived from the signed 8.8% whose provenance (CollecTRI/TRRUST) differs from the unsigned 91.2%. Its values are also nearly degenerate (interquartile range about 0.78-0.92). A null here is a null about THIS feature set on THIS coverage, not a proof that no feature set could work
the DepMap cross-line co-expression feature is not a graph and therefore has no rewiring control of its own; its only control is the swapped-source measurement arm

the rewiring control runs at one CV seed rather than three, and the configuration model can create self-loops and multi-edges, which are kept because removing them would break the exact-degree guarantee the control exists to provide
the RPE1 arm inherits the K562 source->fold assignment rather than re-partitioning, and only 13.4% of unsigned curated edges are testable there, so it is a thinner test than the K562 arm

sources are held out but TARGETS are not: a target gene appears in both training and test folds. That is deliberate -- the target-direction confound is what the swapped-source control removes -- but it means a target-specific model could still leak, which is why arm A is reported separately rather than folded into arm C

the JOINT swapped-source arm is worse balanced on RPE1 than the plain decile arm, because RPE1 has only 2,122 perturbations and the strength x cell-count grid leaves thin cells that fall back to the coarser match. On RPE1 the decile and nearest-neighbour arms are the trustworthy ones; the joint arm is reported because the decision takes the strictest of the three and a badly-matched arm can only make the bar harder

mitochondrial fraction stays imbalanced at |SMD| ~0.19 under ALL THREE matches. It is not matched on, and a perturbation that stresses cells is both a strong perturbation and a high-mito one, so some of what the swapped-source control removes is stress rather than source identity

THE PAIRED SCORING, THE NON-TARGET CEILING CONTROL, ARM B0, THE RPE1 RANK READOUT AND THE NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR AND JOINT SWAPPED-SOURCE ARMS WERE ALL ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN, in response to an adversarial re-read of this module. Every one of them is a tightening rather than a loosening and the strictest number governs every decision, but none was pre-registered and they are reported as post-hoc controls. The decision threshold itself was not changed

THE UNPAIRED INCREMENT IS STILL REPORTED because colab/causal_reg.py and colab/reliable_edges.py use that construction and the numbers have to stay comparable to theirs. It should not be read as an effect size here, and those two modules carry the same row-set defect and should be re-audited

the paired comparison restricts both arms to the rows where the swapped source ALSO responds at |z| >= 2, which is a stress-responsive subset of targets. It is the right comparison because both arms are measured there, but it is a narrower population than the arm's full row set, and the arm's raw accuracy on its own full row set is reported separately as the effect size

the RPE1 ACCURACY numbers cannot measure transfer, because the labelled class prior flips between the lines (32% positive in RPE1 against 60% in K562) and a model thresholded at 0.5 in K562 lands below the RPE1 majority baseline regardless of how well it ranks. Criterion (b) therefore also requires a positive rank increment, and the AUC columns are the ones to read. Only 13.4% of unsigned curated edges are RPE1-testable, so it stays a thin test

a null on this feature set is not a proof that sign is unpredictable. Sequence-level features that were not available here -- the source's DNA-binding domain family, its cofactor complexes from a proteomics resource, promoter motif orientation at the target -- are the obvious next attempt, and the ceiling measurement says there is up to +7 points of source-level signal for them to reach

the imputation is scored against a PERTURBATIONAL sign, which is what a whole-cell model needs but is not the same object as the curated activation/repression statement. An edge whose curated sign is right and whose K562 response is buffered scores as an error here
verdict: NULL: THE 558,005 UNSIGNED EDGES CANNOT BE SIGNED FROM WHAT THE CURATED LAYER KNOWS, AND ON A CORRECTED CONTROL THE NULL IS CLEANER THAN THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS MODULE REPORTED. Held out by SOURCE GENE so no TF is in both train and test, the arm containing NO K562 measurement of any kind (arm B0) reaches 59.5% raw held-out accuracy (AUC 0.523) against a majority-class baseline of 59.6%. Against a strength-matched swapped source measured on THE SAME ROWS it is -2.7 points (decile), -0.3 (nearest-neighbour), -3.0 (joint strength x library size), winning 0% of 20 draws at worst, against the +3.0 required. ALL THREE ARE NEGATIVE. The first version reported +1.3 for the nearest-neighbour arm and concluded that 'the control's construction moves the answer by as much as the effect is worth'; that positive number was an artefact of scoring the arm and its control on different rows, and once they are scored on the same rows the three constructions agree. On RPE1 the rank transfer is dAUC -0.002 against a swapped-source AUC of 0.535 (not detected); the RPE1 ACCURACY of 37.7% is not a transfer measurement at all, because the labelled class prior flips between the lines (32.4% positive in RPE1 against 59.6% in K562) and every arm sits below the RPE1 majority baseline of 67.6%. 0 of the 558,005 unsigned edges reach a confidence bin that is both 65% accurate and +0.05 above its own swapped-source control on the same rows, so none are signed and the layer written is empty by construction. On ALL 20,118 curated edges that already carry a sign, that sign predicts the measured K562 perturbational sign at 52.2% against 50.1% for a strength-matched swapped source measured on the SAME rows -- +2.1 points, 100% of 20 draws won. On the 1,011-edge subset selected post hoc at |z| >= 3 it is 70.9% against 61.0% on the control's rows, +13.5 points -- NOT the +23.4 the unpaired comparison reports, and that subset number belongs to 1,011 edges, not to 20,118. Direction is a real property of a curated edge; it is worth about half what an unpaired control makes it look like. It cannot be answered by lookup: CollecTRI and TRRUST cover 43,348 of the 54,128 SIGNED edges and 0 of the 558,005 unsigned ones -- the signed subset IS those resources, and the unsigned subset is a different, ChIP/motif-shaped compendium. AND THE 'CEILING' THAT THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS MODULE OFFERED AS THE REASON TO TRY HARDER IS NOT REGULATORY SIGNAL AT ALL. Estimating a source's measured direction bias on half its unsigned targets predicts the other half at +7.3 points over the same control -- but estimating that bias from genes that are NOT curated targets of the source, same perturbation row, every curated target excluded, predicts those same held-out true targets at +6.6 points -- 91% of it, from a control that knows nothing about which genes the source regulates, leaving at most 0.7 points that is target-specific. What looked like a source-level ceiling for a future sequence feature to reach is a global up/down shift of one CRISPRi row -- normalisation, stress, growth arrest -- and no property of the TF could predict it, because it is a property of the experiment. That the curated activator fraction correlates with it at Spearman +0.010 (p 0.9) is therefore not a missed opportunity; there was nothing there to see. CONTROLS, FIVE OF THEM, AND THE FIFTH REWROTE THE OTHER FOUR. (i) PAIRING. The swapped-source control is conditioned on |z| >= 2 exactly as the edge arm is -- correctly, because selecting on outcome magnitude inflates agreement -- but that condition moves the control onto DIFFERENT ROWS: only ~21% of the arm's rows survive it, and the survivors are targets that also respond strongly to unrelated perturbations, whose direction is far more consistent. Measured on the control's own rows the arm scores 0.5765 rather than 0.5949. Every increment is therefore reported twice, and the paired one governs: arm B0 moves from -0.0081 (unpaired decile) / +0.0126 (unpaired nearest) to -0.0265 / -0.0032 paired. The nearest-neighbour POSITIVE increment that made the three constructions look like they straddled zero was an artefact of the unequal row sets; paired, all three are negative and the answer is the same whichever match is used. (ii) The target-direction arm -- the confound -- reaches 59.7% raw accuracy on held-out TFs at a paired increment of -2.8 points, which is why 0.5 is the wrong null and why a raw accuracy near 60% here means nothing. (iii) Label-shuffled, whole pipeline rerun: acc 0.5934, AUC 0.5004, paired incr -0.0271, against the real full arm's 0.6029 / 0.5443 / -0.0197. (iv) Degree-matched configuration-model rewiring, 20 draws with source out-degree and target in-degree preserved EXACTLY, leaves the source+edge arm at paired incr -0.0233 against the real -0.0265; the real wiring beats the rewired control in 25% of draws on increment and 40% on accuracy, so the little the features do carry is degree, not connectivity. (v) The matched control still fails its own imbalance audit: strength |SMD| 0.25 under a decile match (curated sources are TFs and sit at the top of whatever decile they land in), 0.23 under nearest-neighbour-in-strength, 0.22 under a joint strength x library-size match, with mitochondrial fraction stuck near 0.19 under all three. Those tightenings are why three constructions are reported; PAIRING, not matching, turned out to be what moved the answer. colab/causal_reg.py and colab/reliable_edges.py use the unpaired decile-matched construction and should be re-audited for the same row-set defect -- their increments are large enough that a 2-point shift would not overturn them, but it should be stated. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN THE FIRST VERSION CLAIMED. The measured layer already answers this for the edges it can reach: colab/causal_reg.py carries a K562 perturbational sign for every (perturbation, gene) pair it measures, and 360,946 of the 612,133 curated triples (59%) fall inside that matrix -- 340,826 of them currently unsigned. Signing a curated edge is a measurement problem, not an inference problem, and the honest coverage statement for this project is 59% by measurement and 0% by imputation. The first version pointed at sequence-level features and a '+7.6 point source-level ceiling' as the obvious next attempt; the non-target control above removes that motivation, because the ceiling is a property of the perturbation row and not of the TF. The route that would extend coverage is more perturbation atlases: the unsigned edges whose source is never perturbed anywhere are the ones that stay dark.

     one half, predict the other. Its control is the same swapped-source arm.

(ii) The target-direction arm -- the confound -- reaches 59.7% raw accuracy on held-out TFs at a paired increment of -2.8 points, which is why 0.5 is the wrong null and why a raw accuracy near 60% here means nothing. (iii) Label-shuffled, whole pipeline rerun: acc 0.5934, AUC 0.5004, paired incr -0.0271, against the real full arm's 0.6029 / 0.5443 / -0.0197. (iv) Degree-matched configuration-model rewiring, 20 draws with source out-degree and target in-degree preserved EXACTLY, leaves the source+edge arm at paired incr -0.0233 against the real -0.0265; the real wiring beats the rewired control in 25% of draws on increment and 40% on accuracy, so the little the features do carry is degree, not connectivity. (v) The matched control still fails its own imbalance audit: strength |SMD| 0.25 under a decile match (curated sources are TFs and sit at the top of whatever decile they land in), 0.23 under nearest-neighbour-in-strength, 0.22 under a joint strength x library-size match, with mitochondrial fraction stuck near 0.19 under all three. Those tightenings are why three constructions are reported; PAIRING, not matching, turned out to be what moved the answer. colab/causal_reg.py and colab/reliable_edges.py use the unpaired decile-matched construction and should be re-audited for the same row-set defect -- their increments are large enough that a 2-point shift would not overturn them, but it should be stated. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN THE FIRST VERSION CLAIMED. The measured layer already answers this for the edges it can reach: colab/causal_reg.py carries a K562 perturbational sign for every (perturbation, gene) pair it measures, and 360,946 of the 612,133 curated triples (59%) fall inside that matrix -- 340,826 of them currently unsigned. Signing a curated edge is a measurement problem, not an inference problem, and the honest coverage statement for this project is 59% by measurement and 0% by imputation. The first version pointed at sequence-level features and a '+7.6 point source-level ceiling' as the obvious next attempt; the non-target control above removes that motivation, because the ceiling is a property of the perturbation row and not of the TF. The route that would extend coverage is more perturbation atlases: the unsigned edges whose source is never perturbed anywhere are the ones that stay dark.
